original_test_intent: Exercise the DDR5 PMIC current-limiter warning for every approved target and voltage type, verify the approved correctable/fatal handling and OS evidence, then prove the limiter state clears with no unintended clamp, trip, reset or memory degradation.
original_method: Prove railtype11/voltagetype meanings and the PMIC limiter state machine; map DIMMs, rails, sensors and I2C access; record current/voltage/thermal baselines; inject one tuple; correlate raw warning/limiter bits with calibrated telemetry and fresh RAS records; verify assert/clear timing and recovery before moving to another target.
manual_activity: The PMIC/power owner identifies whether railtype11 asserts a pre-limit warning or active limiter, approves safe thresholds and targets, supervises one injection and restores the electrical and memory state.
required_inputs: Vendor proof for railtype11 and voltagetype0/1 plus warning/status/clamp/trip meanings
Approved correctable/fatal severity, reset policy, assert/deassert thresholds, hysteresis, latch and timing
Wistron BMC/platform I2C controller, bus, address, registers and independent OOB path
Joined command form and complete enumerated tuple matrix
Calibrated current/voltage/thermal limits, PMIC/CPER/SEL oracle, recovery and restoration criteria
safety_requirements: Use a dedicated recoverable SUT with independent OOB and calibrated current, voltage and temperature capture
Keep stimulus within vendor-approved synthetic-injection limits; do not create physical overcurrent to obtain a warning
Run one mapped tuple once and abort on actual clamp/trip, rail droop, temperature excursion, reset, I2C loss or memory error
Capture raw status before any approved clear and confirm limiter state, rails and memory have returned to baseline
Restore all PMIC recovery/mode, SPD-control, telemetry, I2C and HDT settings
agent_execution_scope: Check the approved limiter state definition, mapping, thresholds, evidence and recovery plan
Collect read-only raw limiter status, current/rail/thermal/fan telemetry, event timeline, CPER/SEL and memory health
Do not configure PMIC/I2C/BIOS/HDT, inject, induce current, clear, reset, recover, repeat or determine PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Resolve warning versus active limiting and Fatal versus correctable semantics
Approve target/register/sensor matrix and safe synthetic stimulus
Restore state and judge each tuple

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A grep for current.limit can neither identify the PMIC/rail nor distinguish a warning bit from active current limiting or trip.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After the railtype11 state machine and matrix are approved, inject one tuple while synchronizing raw status and calibrated electrical telemetry, then verify clear and full recovery.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: listvalidumc, 0:0:3, railtype11, voltagetype0/1, dimm0, Fatal label, correctable Criteria, all-DIMM repetition, PMIC/I2C settings and 360/120 minutes are preserved as source facts.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Validate one synthetic limiter-warning assertion per mapped PMIC with raw status and calibrated telemetry, without producing an unapproved physical clamp or trip.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines warning/clamp/trip boundaries, state timing, target registers, independent interlocks, recovery and restoration.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Tool PASS and OS logging do not demonstrate which limiter state occurred or whether rail delivery and memory remained within limits.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: An incorrect threshold or tuple may actively current-limit a DIMM rail and cause training errors, shutdown or damage.

project_override_considerations: The platform PMIC register map and independent current instrumentation govern acceptance; host logs alone cannot establish limiter state. I2C ownership stays with the Wistron BMC/platform path.
expected_evidence: Authoritative railtype11/parameter and warning/clamp/trip state definitions plus full physical topology
Pinned tool/spec, raw register baseline and calibrated current/voltage/thermal baseline
Exact one-shot injection with synchronized status and telemetry timeline
Fresh target-specific PMIC and CPER/SEL evidence showing the approved state and power-action outcome
Deasserted/cleared limiter state, stable rails/thermals, restored DIMM inventory and clean memory health
Configuration restoration diff and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The procedure calls the action Fatal while the item calls it a warning and Criteria calls it correctable. It never distinguishes pre-limit warning from active limiting/trip, and the fixed tuple cannot prove the requested all-DIMM/dual-voltage coverage.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Static review can preserve the limiter-warning intent and identify missing decisions. Only execution remains gated on the vendor state definition, safe stimulus and platform mapping.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 99 Wistron-System RAS-00819-V002: prove railtype11 selects Current Limiter Warning and define voltagetype0/1; distinguish pre-limit warning, active clamp and trip; reconcile Fatal label with correctable Criteria and reset/no-reset behavior; map every DIMM/PMIC/rail/current sensor plus Wistron BMC/platform I2C controller/bus/address/register/OOB path; approve command/tuple matrix, thresholds, hysteresis/latch/clear timing, safe limits, PMIC/CPER/SEL evidence, memory recovery, aborts and restoration.

review_improvement: Introduces a limiter state-machine oracle so a generic warning log cannot be mistaken for current clamp, trip or successful recovery.
independent_technical_reasoning: A limiter warning can precede, accompany or merely predict current clamping depending on the PMIC. Those states have different safety and recovery implications. Because the source mixes Fatal, warning and correctable language, acceptance requires vendor register semantics, measured rail behavior and an explicit reset policy rather than a tool PASS alone.
